# B01 1.0.1 source-bound native acceptance — 2026-09-29

## Decision and limits

`native_behavior_accepted` and `reusable_published` for fixed, positive-duration
preparation on the A01 normal path. The [observable contract](contract.json),
fresh native run and [independent read-only replay](review/independent-readonly-rerun-2026-09-29.json)
all pass with zero differences. PR #44 permits complete source-bound CLI
behavior evidence without a universal GUI screenshot gate.

This evidence does not prove an internal preparation-object creation count or
a causal launch delay: preparation ends before the scheduled 08:00 launch. It
does not establish GUI-only behavior, resource contention, B02, Python/Rust
parity or aircraft types beyond the generic teaching asset. The original B01
1.0.0 model remains `not_published` with separate historical evidence.

# B02 1.0.2 source-bound native review — 2026-09-29

## Decision and scope

`native_behavior_accepted` and `reusable_published` for two strictly serial preparation steps on the published B01 1.0.1 one-aircraft normal path. The raw run's historical `candidate_cli_review` and `not_published` fields record its pre-review state and are unchanged.

This evidence does not establish resource waiting, a causal launch delay, random work, arbitrary parallel task graphs, GUI-only behavior, cross-engine parity or performance. The native event log names subtask ordinals and SEQ values; `INSPECT` and `SERVICE` are bound to those SEQ values by the source and roundtrip rows. # B04 cross-midnight turnround: CLI scope signoff

**Decision:** `native_behavior_accepted` for the paired, deterministic one-aircraft behavior below; `reusable_published` after merge to `simlox/main`. This does not complete the full B04 catalog case or its variants.

The accepted parent is published B02 1.0.2 (input SHA-256 `fc9e80de0ac8515f3d3a7fe4a2c9aa916bce23ba5b05e13e2f69857230d9dc34`); the A02 repeated-mission prerequisite is also published. Frozen `control-input.json` and `turnround-input.json` SHA-256 values are `9cc5c39a6d2d93b98c03fc0c483bf90963a76e67be6953444003f30bfa8dd98c` and `9f985c071d7d1958b55659f8ae39bc4c47580847d3bf6057d5e01f483004a9c5`. The [exact source diff](exact-diff.json) SHA-256 is `b13bdadbeeda7c7a38bec265882eaee53e3d3d3546748a641f5d06d322942f17`; the frozen [contract](contract.json) SHA-256 is `d65cef9a589fef1234bc1d09c649c61af31190ea867c8d7c4a106aa43f1fb6ca`. Relative to B02, both inputs schedule waves at 21.5 and 24.75 hours with a one-hour second-wave delay allowance. Only the child adds one one-hour `MissionTurnround` row. The installed 2017 manual SHA-256 is `39427027c46809a9ce9ebcb9be04e7396d96746e42a6f8c7c0ba2ddc294ef8a3`; printed pages 181–183 and 305–307 describe the relevant preparation and post-mission work.

Sealed session-0 SSH native runs `b04-v101-control-20260930-01` and `b04-v101-turnround-20260930-01` have closure SHA-256 `c1c99765128e22ed73cba808fe019f1b943f95596f8ffb79aff8033781d609d4` and `85d25bd8fa2a053639ca9a93b3bbdd78a5c04e3db9a5d826e27998d500f95ae1`. Both completed guarded import, export, calculation, JSON report and source roundtrip with the global Issue #18 mutex and GUI PID 13340/session 1 preserved. All 17/18 populated business source tables roundtripped exactly; conversion had zero errors and warnings #108/#126.

| Event | Control | One-hour turnround |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First preparation and mission | 20.5–21; 21.5–23.5 | 20.5–21; 21.5–23.5 |
| First post-flight turnround | Instantaneous markers at 23.5 | 23.5–24.5, crossing midnight |
| Second notice/preassignment | 23.75 | 23.75 |
| Second allocation and preparation | 23.75; 23.75–24.25 | 24.5; 24.5–25 |
| Second mission and completion | 24.75–26.75 | 25–27 |
| Second post-flight turnround | Instantaneous markers at 26.75 | 27–28 |

The same `<TEACH-AIR-01,0>` flies both missions in each run. Both missions succeed in both runs. The 72 half-hour system bins integrate to four aircraft mission-hours and one preparation hour in each; `NSYMT` integrates to zero versus two turnround hours. The 72 stock bins show no demand, movement or waiting, with one aircraft ready at the hour-36 end. The observed 0.25-hour second-launch shift follows release from turnround, rather than a stock or maintenance interruption. Internal scheduling order at the same timestamp is not directly exposed.

The [author validator](validate_native.py) SHA-256 is `c48ec0e36ec42fb8929c3e156a0adfec1d4fc738bb7072e3123dddd4c9d61866`, and its [passing report](review/author-native-validation-2026-09-30.json) SHA-256 is `4d13b9e096a4f827a9ad0acf48772c8b906edad38f56636ffefb9a1adaa24832`. The separate standard-library [read-only reviewer](review/independent_turnround_readonly.py) did not import the author implementation or invoke SIMLOX. Its script SHA-256 is `6f585f0e03c645a55b50b563d539124da276437c3e9a7126dcf88958e5012fbe`; its [72/72 passing report](review/independent-turnround-2026-09-30.json) SHA-256 is `a3bf505aa878a33f5da64f386d47c7930140bb1284da1200f94bc228a73e1b80`.

Raw native outputs remain in local ignored `runs/`. A prior local v1.0.0 probe retained the inherited 0.333333-hour second-wave allowance and cancelled that wave at 24.3333, before turnround ended at 24.5. It failed its predicted-success contract and is excluded. This signoff covers one aircraft/type, fixed durations and allowance, with no resource demand, repair or PM. Waiting turnround, exact day-boundary equality, arbitrary preparation overlap, GUI-only behavior and cross-engine parity remain unverified.

# D01 1.0.0: system-level direct repair, restricted CLI sign-off

## Decision and source

`native_behavior_accepted_cli_scope` and `reusable_published` **only for
the single-aircraft system-level direct-repair recipe** below. This is a
restricted first D01 slice, not acceptance of the catalog's installed-item
failure, item replacement or ItemRepair scope. It derives from the
[published A02 repeated-mission case](../A02-single-aircraft-repeated-missions/cli-scope-signoff-2026-09-29.md),
parent input SHA-256
`84c5cca6c06384b850d2420297a3f5c2f5c553904f123f690190fdb42475e0b8`.
The frozen [D01 input](native-input.json), SHA-256
`d418c811f2e1a9ad047af19038a3d0881d404adf0919d2e52dab70e6100ee450`,
changes only `ProblemDescription`, `System.FRT` and `SystemRepair`; the
[parent diff](parent-diff.json) lists every changed row. The frozen
[contract](contract.json) SHA-256 is
`3058fb0e29e3bb89449485b94ab92b372affd80660bb997a22d30d30816394eb`.

The installed SIMLOX 2017 manual, SHA-256
`39427027c46809a9ce9ebcb9be04e7396d96746e42a6f8c7c0ba2ddc294ef8a3`,
describes operational FRT as failures per million OPIDs on physical PDF
pages 240, 246 and 258; `System.FRT=300000` with `OPID=OPHOURS` therefore
specifies 0.3 failures per operating hour. Pages 190–191 and 211–212
describe traditional critical direct system failures and repair tasks;
pages 349–354 define `SystemRepair` at a workstation and `DIRPT` as total
turnaround time. No proprietary manual page is stored in the repository.

## Sealed native behavior

The four-step session-0 SSH run `d01-v100-ssh-20260929-01` remains in the
case's local ignored `runs/` directory. The [runner](run_native_ssh.ps1),
SHA-256 `07a152c54e72da4fd024839bb98037f3f5c282c7eebecc5e6ca317fbcc389a70`,
serialized the native calls under the host-wide queue and preserved GUI
PID 13340, session 1 and its start identity. All import, export,
calculation and report-export steps exited zero. The invocation SHA-256 is
`cad80021f770db3acb7af5f64a029f8af24b2aa44d41f439685f7e052405c8c4`;
the raw closure SHA-256 is
`c3769da04ae3e8e754ff172cb0bed9317a0ec7ec5352913086341cc0ad489c05`.
The SXI SHA-256 is
`ff465ca4b4ab1f0f9a61a32ea0c7121c8c87cf7547c8a2d36d70c72eb44294dc`,
the event log SHA-256 is
`71c46a192990c81bf27ed6fd1b41ea15b5ada25834131a7700d4d1b779e83161`,
and the raw JSON report SHA-256 is
`cb21d4b6f7c3c35b8d42412e60bb6ca85d178b4ef6e9d61d71ca294ba94fc83a`.

All supplied rows survived native import/export; the extra rows are
SIMLOX-generated default table values. Conversion had zero errors and only
warnings 108 (logging) and 126 (system contains no installed items). The
fixed seed produced two **observed** critical failures at hours 9.8829 and
33.8602 on `<TEACH-AIR-01,0>`, aborting the 08:00 and 32:00 missions.
Each aircraft returned to `BASE-01` at hours 10 and 34, entered a local
system direct-repair task without resource demand, completed a 0.5-hour
turnaround at 10.5 and 34.5, and became ready again. The middle 20:00
mission completed successfully at 22:00. There was no cancellation.

The report has 72 half-hour SystemResults intervals, two failure counts,
two repair counts, two half-hour repair windows and one aircraft ready at
hour 36. Mission success fraction is approximately 1/3; the sealed
[A02 no-fault control](../A02-single-aircraft-repeated-missions/cli-scope-signoff-2026-09-29.md)
has 3/3 success, zero failures and zero repairs under the same three-wave
schedule. Its report SHA-256 is
`a7227687988841c074b28b524792af7d856cd674840169bf15c210f2d2cd4739`.
The six changed half-hour SystemResults rows begin at 9.5, 10, 10.5,
33.5, 34 and 34.5 hours. The coarse report still totals six nominal
mission-operation hours even though two missions aborted late; exact abort
times come from the event log, not that aggregate duration.

The [author validator](validate_native_cli.py), SHA-256
`bb29231b1aaf3a43054e6c345f2b4f3457c768ea4d31cca42bb517e74bcbb579`,
passed 293 source-bound checks; its [result](review/author-validation-2026-09-29.json)
SHA-256 is
`7f040f107675348511be04150a8ec9cbdd234d77bb01ee11269ccd6f00fdcae4`.
The separate [read-only reviewer](review/independent_readonly.py), SHA-256
`72df60b990fcaa8361dfefd974e2a1ca97a7103c4789bb155ef02c9f0c1fdca7`,
imports no author validator and replayed the raw seals, parent delta,
source bindings, process provenance, roundtrip, events and report against
the A02 control. Its [result](review/independent-readonly-2026-09-29.json),
SHA-256 `7198b785f80e2e6cb5db51940a237a87b097760169aae33aa186373b6ab4d4f0`,
passed with `differences=[]`.

## Restricted and unverified

The two failure times are run-specific observations for seed 1 and this
executable, not scheduled inputs or a portable random-stream guarantee.
`DIRPT=0.5 h` is total repair turnaround, not a separately measured wrench
time. There is no installed component in this model; item failure,
replacement, `ItemRepair`, stock and resupply remain unverified D01
extensions. No resource contention, PM, explicit failure mode, GUI-only
behavior or cross-engine equivalence is accepted. GUI preservation is
recorded by the bound runner; GUI window content was not sampled. The
original contract and native run say `not_published` because they were
created as a candidate; this dated sign-off is the restricted publication
decision.

# D03 calendar PM: CLI scope sign-off (2026-09-30)

**Decision:** `native_behavior_accepted_cli_scope`, `reusable_published` for one generic aircraft, three nonoverlapping missions, and a fixed one-hour preventive maintenance task triggered by a 24-hour calendar interval. This is a bounded native SIMLOX result, not an assertion about PM under mission conflict, resource shortages, item replacement, alternative operation parameters, or a third cycle beyond the 60-hour horizon.

## Source and execution

The accepted [A02 parent](../A02-single-aircraft-repeated-missions/cli-scope-signoff-2026-09-29.md) input SHA-256 is `84c5cca6c06384b850d2420297a3f5c2f5c553904f123f690190fdb42475e0b8`. Frozen [D03 input](native-input.json) SHA-256 is `5f2f74e6fe19df29d691ca44601a04a8c9a3663cbeca07f33c18a01b7c0f1a32`; the [parent diff](parent-diff.json) changes `Control.SIMPE/RCEND` and `ResultCollection.RCEND` from 36 to 60 hours, `Control.ENPM` from `N` to `Y`, and adds one row each to `Tasks`, `MaterielPM`, `PMLocation`, `SubTaskType`, and `TaskBreakDown`. `MaterielPM` uses `PMINT=24`, `OPID=CALHOURS`, `ATIM=DTIM=0`. The local `PMLocation` links a one-hour `INSPECT` subtask. The installed manual explains the relevant fields on pages 202–204, 370–375, 387–389 and 402–404; native timing is established by the run.

The [contract](contract.json) SHA-256 is `3a231facf94971a619189e75c4e5d65a375e8f0eebb20da7db3a49426e7cfc92`. The first native pilot showed that A02's `ResultCollection` still ended at hour 36 and showed the second PM at hour 49. Before the accepted run, both result-window rows were extended to hour 60 and the contract recorded the pilot's observed second start. The pilot is not used as final report evidence.

Accepted run `d03-calendar-v100-ssh-20261001-02` used session-0 SSH, the host-wide `Global\SimloxIssue18NativeQueue` mutex and the active GUI PID 13340 guard. Import, export, calculation, JSON report and roundtrip checker all exited zero. All 18 populated source tables roundtripped identically. Conversion had zero errors and two expected warnings: `#108` for event logging and `#126` for the intentionally item-free aircraft. Sealed invocation SHA-256 is `aee0b3e23739d82bdaef3597712ee7db09ca51060b0e781e3c61e61d50046b91`; closure SHA-256 is `9cd845f957105eb8659809ec09cf380ae5df68a63babb264d70631c164f7d2d8`. Raw native files remain in ignored local `runs/d03-calendar-v100-ssh-20261001-02/`.

## Observed behavior and report

The event log records a `CAL24` system PM task and its sole one-hour subtask starting at hour 24 and completing at 25; the aircraft leaves ready status during this task and returns ready at 25. The next `CAL24` task starts at hour 49 and completes at 50, again returning the aircraft ready. The second start is 24 hours after the first completion in this run. The log does not expose the scheduler's internal rule, so completion-based rescheduling is an inference rather than a general PM guarantee. Both tasks request no resources. # D06 explicit position failure mode: CLI scope sign-off (2026-09-30)

**Decision:** `native_behavior_accepted_cli_scope`, `reusable_published` for one explicit FMID on the first of two positions holding the same LRU type, with local direct system CM. This is a bounded D06 foundation; other failure modes and replacement behavior remain planned.

## Source and native run

The accepted [D01 installed-LRU parent](../D01-installed-lru-direct-repair-v1.0.0/cli-scope-signoff-2026-09-29.md) input SHA-256 is `eb57ef7bdb9829241303d3827c10ef957e6bb5e8f4f5f6034bb6f5dc603b3b93`. The [D06 input](native-input.json) SHA-256 is `ee7484a32492d1aa6cd90ad961620ecdd3de1244f09b16ba4a96a2978310ce78`; the [exact parent diff](parent-diff.json), SHA-256 `b878916c46ae14b7e989adea493dcfb424ac13d8becc18a1d887ea53e493366d`, changes seven parent tables and adds `MaterielPosition`, `MaterielStructure`, `FailureMode` and `CMLocation`, leaving 24 parent tables unchanged. The two positions `POS-A` and `POS-B` each hold `TEACH-LRU-01`. `FM-POS-A` has `FRQ=300000` per million `OPHOURS` and `CRITF=1`. `CMLocation` maps it to `TEACH-AIR-01` at `BASE-01` for `CMT=0.5` hours. Both traditional FRT fields are null, and the traditional structure, repair and stock rows are empty. The [contract](contract.json) states the predeclared hypothesis and limits.

The installed SIMLOX 2017 manual, SHA-256 `39427027c46809a9ce9ebcb9be04e7396d96746e42a6f8c7c0ba2ddc294ef8a3`, pages 355–357 and 364–370, documents failure-mode CM mapping, position-linked modes and avoiding traditional FRT for explicitly modeled items. The installed field dictionary was supplemented by the native exporter's optional `RUBM`, `CMM` and `CMC` columns. Neither proprietary source is uploaded.

Accepted native run ID `d06-position-cm-v100-ssh-20260930-02` used session-0 SSH, the host-wide `Global\SimloxIssue18NativeQueue`, and the active GUI PID 13340 guard. Import, export, calculation, report and roundtrip checker all exited zero. All 18 source row-containing tables roundtripped exactly, including three all-null placeholder rows. Conversion had **zero errors and one warning**, #108 for event logging. Raw artifacts remain in ignored local `runs/`.

| Accepted raw artifact | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `invocation.json` | `db8925c06d1ca4a5d74f5d022d8eb919f68d375db3ed5f9d35693ef84c903108` |
| `closure.json` | `afd8689161874d247dee92a6f6265211733375b8933f3fcd30bfb297cfe975c7` |
| `model.log` | `92930370c7a60faa7870fa4fb43fffad73d2c3582e187c39506927012198ae1a` |
| `report-raw.json` | `230403de72c36ae2ba2b6e57939ef9dd94571f94de840fa718084736e93630b8` |

## Observed behavior and review

Native events show critical `FM-POS-A` failures on `POS-A` at 9.8829 and 33.8602 hours. Both abort the current mission. On returns at 10 and 34, the aircraft starts system CM tasks bearing `FM-POS-A`; they complete at 10.5 and 34.5. The middle mission succeeds at 22. Across 72 half-hour bins, `NFAIL=2` and `NREPT=2`, with one aircraft-hour in repair and one ready aircraft at the hour-36 stop. The explicit input has no traditional FRT branch, and all observed failure/repair counts reconcile to the two FMID events. The native log names the affected position; the same-LRU placement at both positions is evidenced by the input and its roundtrip, not by an isolated failure at `POS-B`.

The [author replay](review/author-position-validation-2026-09-30.json) passed **60/60** checks, SHA-256 `fdf10f1bc28af643424e4f33d69bcd0f158c5e69ca2635a6c7f69f245e2b1eae`. Its [validator](validate_position.py) SHA-256 is `dc94ba182763d9143391e748690293b5819b1c96eb706c144bf8b73c9f13918d`. A separate reviewer wrote a [read-only replay](review/independent_position_readonly.py), SHA-256 `7ddd5e4764465a95dbd1bd51be0fa74dce86e1ce7b68d5482cbc00fbb070bebcd`, without importing the author validator. Its [76/76 result](review/independent-position-2026-09-30.json), SHA-256 `6ba8f422c80c78695a5005ea29a6465e8df0816bb06fbfaa3142fc4b2eb82627`, agrees with the exact delta, sealed native raw data, FMID/position/CM mapping and report totals.

The earlier immutable run `d06-position-cm-v100-ssh-20260930-01` is excluded. Its source input SHA-256 was `bac738acdfb0e869549a858be8f63fd39de45d686907af7e25e19c232e253ad8`; the roundtrip checker exited 1 because the native exporter added the three optional columns absent from that input. Its native event log and report hashes match the accepted run, but a successful simulation alone did not meet the frozen identity check.

This result does not establish `POS-B` failure behavior, position-specific alternative maintenance, multiple modes, item replacement or stock effects, `CMRF`/`CMRQ`/`CMRQD`, resources, GUI visual content or cross-engine equivalence. The GUI identity and active session were guarded, but visual content was not sampled. Issue #18 stays open.

# E05 local LRU repair, restock and reissue: CLI scope sign-off (2026-09-29)

**Decision:** `native_behavior_accepted_cli_scope`, `reusable_published` for one local LRU repair loop whose repaired item is issued on a later demand. The pinned run produced three complete cycles, all of which are traced. This does not accept a shortage, late repair/backorder, remote supply, reorder, resource competition or PM case.

## Frozen source and execution

This case derives from accepted E01 input SHA-256 `84ca1828f3669d2c91c9d826cae3187e0968ae9f8fed602d97155d2e82e99931`. The [parent diff](parent-diff.json) changes only `ProblemDescription`, `System.FRT` and `Item.FRT`, raising the equal traditional `OPHOURS` rates from 300000 to 450000 per million. Installed SIMLOX executable SHA-256 is `fe24c5bffc0c0641894bb335484cfb83993e3db2bd60122ddadfedd39a8c4db0`; installed manual SHA-256 is `39427027c46809a9ce9ebcb9be04e7396d96746e42a6f8c7c0ba2ddc294ef8a3`.

Native run `e05-v100-ssh-20260929-01` used session-0 SSH, the host-wide `Global\SimloxIssue18NativeQueue` mutex and active GUI PID 13340 guard. Import, export, calculation and report export exited zero; 20 row-containing source tables, including three all-null placeholder tables, roundtripped identically. Conversion had zero errors and only logging warning 108. Sealed invocation SHA-256 is `a5e5b85421c0d25d1779fad20da0eb7acbb98ea03a347591436157930704bbac`; closure SHA-256 is `e75836bcd99ba838d4ef247973794a2bf38fbddd4904d69337d631ba983d01ef`. Raw evidence stays in the ignored local `runs/e05-v100-ssh-20260929-01/` directory.

## Observed material loop

| Wave | Critical LRU failure | Demand and local issue | Removed item reaches repair | System ready | Repaired item restocked |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 9.25527 | 9.75527: issue spare instance 0 for failed instance 1 | 9.92193 | 10.2553 | instance 1 at 10.9219 |
| 2 | 21.9597 | 22: issue **repaired instance 1** for failed instance 2 | 22.1667 | 22.5 | instance 2 at 23.1667 |
| 3 | 33.3079 | 33.8079: issue **repaired instance 2** for failed instance 3 | 33.9746 | 34.3079 | instance 3 at 34.9746 |

Every failure aborts its scheduled mission. Each system replacement performs explicit 10-minute `<REMOVE>` and 20-minute `<REPLACE>` in sequence; the removed item starts one-hour direct `ItemRepair` at removal completion. The stock event ledger shows on hand `1→0→1` in each cycle, without backorders. In particular, instance 1 completed repair and returned to stock at 10.9219, well before it was issued on the second demand at 22. The extra third cycle also completed before the 36-hour horizon.

The fractional repair-occupancy bins integrate to 1.5 aircraft-hours of system replacement. The accepted E01 control had one failure/repair/demand and two successful missions; E05 adds two of each and all three missions abort. Exact item identity and transition times come from the event log; the report provides aggregate intervals and rounds times differently.

## Review and limits

The [author replay](review/author-native-validation-2026-09-29.json) passed 79 source-bound checks with no differences. A separate reviewer performed [static prelaunch review](review/static-review-2026-09-29.md) and [independent read-only native replay](review/independent-native-review-2026-09-29.json), with no differences. The independent report SHA-256 is `ad7801108647a3cb0790a0d93abf85f45c5613377b0dcfb7e6f58d0c59026936`. The independent replay checked frozen inputs, three-table delta, every sealed raw hash, SSH/GUI records, three identity-matched material loops, report totals and the E01 control.

The contract required at least two failures and complete tracing of any additional failure. Three occurred on this executable and all three are covered. The rate and seed do not prescribe the failure count or timestamps on other executables. GUI visual content was not sampled.

The control and child roundtrip all 16/17 authored row-containing tables. Both converters report zero errors. The attrition control logs BATTLE-LOSS and permanent loss h8.78145, an aborted first mission, and later mission cancellations. The system child logs BATTLE-LOSS and aborts at h8.78145, h21.1446 and h32.1965. Local system DIRP tasks begin at h9.28145, h21.6446 and h32.393; each plans one hour and completes at h10.2814, h22.6446 and h33.393. Readiness is restored at those completion times. The second and third missions launch at h20 and h32; no mission succeeds because each launched mission is damaged and aborted.

Both reports contain 72 aligned half-hour System and Stock bins and one ResultSummary row. Control lost-aircraft exposure integrates 27.21855 hours through h36 and ends lost1/ready0. ## Limits

The IID change and new damage repair row are coupled in this pair. One seed and one generic airframe without items do not test damaged LRU/SRU behavior, repair fraction, shortages, other direct or system repair choices, visual GUI behavior or cross-engine parity.
